pageCache.pageTitle: Southrop C of E Primary School - Home Page
pageCache.text:
A Church of England primary in a beautiful village setting. A small school with a rich extra-curricular offering where children achieve and flourish.
Welcome to Southrop C of E Primary School
Southrop is a Church of England school that draws pupils from Gloucestershire, Oxfordshire and Wiltshire. The school has a high ratio of staff to children and has a strong academic record. We are proud of our results, but we also recognise that primary education is not simply an academic experience. Enjoyment, wellbeing, emotional development and an understanding of the way the world works are at the core of a Southrop education – as are opportunities for children to take part in a wide range of extra-curricular activities.
Noticeboard

pageCache.pageTitle: Southrop C of E Primary School - Breakfast club/after-school care
pageCache.text:
Breakfast club/After-school care
We offer Breakfast Club this from 8am until 8.30am, Monday to Friday. The children can arrive at any point during this period, for a piece of toast, a play outside with friends or some quiet activities inside. What a great start to the day!
We offer childcare from 3 until 5pm every week day during term time (with certain exceptions during the year). This gives the children the chance to spend time with either an after school playleader or a sports coach doing things that excite them.
Mrs Martyn, our After School Club Playleader, is always full of new ideas. Whenever possible she likes to get the children outside in the playground or wildlife garden. They may be using the trim trail, bikes, gardening, creating fairy gardens and much more! She also does craft activities, cookery and hugely popular junk modelling sessions. On the days that we are up at the Jubilee Field for PE, After School Club will take place there too.
Contact the school office for details of costs and how to make a booking.

pageCache.pageTitle: Southrop C of E Primary School - Applying for a place
pageCache.text:
Open events
We hold a number of Open Days throughout the year, offering families the opportunity to explore our school and experience our welcoming environment. For those considering a Reception place for September, our Open Days are a great way to see what we offer and meet our staff. If you are unable to attend one of these events, we are very happy to arrange an individual tour at a time that suits you. We also welcome enquiries for in-year admissions, and encourage families to visit us at any point during the school year.
To arrange a tour or to find out more about any aspect of the admissions process, please contact the school office on 01367 850246.
How and when to apply
Children normally start school in the September following their fourth birthday. The window for applying for a place opens at the end of October and shuts in the middle of January. This time around, the window opens on November 3rd 20205 and shuts on January 15th 2025.
Parents are encouraged to list five preferred schools on their form as school places cannot be guaranteed. Failing to include second, third, fourth and fifth preferences could lead to children being allocated school places that parents would not have listed.
All applications for places need to be made through your local county council.
Gloucestershire County Council.
https://www.gloucestershire.gov.uk/education-and-learning/school-admissions/admissions-to-reception-at-primary-school-3-junior-school-lower-to-middle-school-places-for-september-2024/
Oxfordshire County Council
https://www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/schools/apply-school-place/reception-applications
Wiltshire County Council
https://www.wiltshire.gov.uk/article/1657/Apply-for-a-school-place
Swindon Borough Council
https://www.swindon.gov.uk/info/20071/school_places_and_admissions/427/primary_school_places_and_admissions
Admissions Policy Sept 2025
What happens after you have applied?
Parents/carers will find out which school they have been allocated on April 16th 2026 and will need to accept the place by April 23rd.
Parents/carers who request to go on a waiting list for a school (in the hope that not all children allocated places go on to accept them) or who have made a late application will find out if they have a place at their preferred school on or immediately after May 14th.
The appeals process
If you have not been allocated a place at the school of your choice, then you can appeal to Gloucestershire County Council. All the relevant information about this process can be found here:Gloucestershire County Councils Appeals process
Appeals can be heard during June and July.
Transferring from another school
For pupils already at school and seeking a place at Southrop, admissions are managed by the school itself. You should telephone the school to enquire about vacancies. If we have space, then you will be asked to come to meet the Headteacher so that we can fully understand your child.
You are then welcome to make an application on the form downloadable here: https://www.gloucestershire.gov.uk/education-and-learning/school-admissions/applying-for-a-school-place-during-the-school-year/
In the event that a place cannot be offered, you will be given advice about how the In-Year Admissions team at Gloucestershire County Council can help you with either an appeal or to find a place in an alternative school.
